info.title: Connect Trade API
info.description:
# Getting Started
Welcome to the Connect Trade API.

Here you’ll find the technical details for our endpoints, data models, and authentication flows needed to integrate broker trading and account access into your platform.

# Authentication
Authenticate every request with credential headers:
- **Platform endpoints** (e.g. user management): `client-id` and `client-secret`.
- **User endpoints** (connections, accounts, balances, orders, positions, transactions): `client-id` and `client-secret`, plus the `user-id` and `user-secret` of the user you act for.

```shell
curl --request GET \
--url 'https://api.connecttrade.com/accounts' \
--header 'client-id: YOUR_CLIENT_ID' \
--header 'client-secret: YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET' \
--header 'user-id: USER_ID' \
--header 'user-secret: USER_SECRET'
```

Each endpoint lists the headers it needs under **Authorizations**. Keep your secrets on your server and never send them to a browser or mobile app.

For direct browser or client-side access, see [Access Tokens](#tag/Access-Tokens).

tags.name: Access Tokens
tags.description:
**Optional.** Every endpoint works with the [credential headers](#section/Authentication). You only need access tokens when a browser or another front end calls Connect Trade directly, so your secrets never leave your server.

### When to use access tokens
- **User access token:** your front end acts for one user, e.g. shows their accounts or places orders. The token carries `read` and/or `trade` scopes and only works for that user's endpoints.
- **Platform access token:** your front end covers many users, e.g. an admin UI or a dashboard that streams updates for many users, without exposing your `client-secret`.

### When you don't need them
Server-to-server integrations. If only your backend calls Connect Trade, keep using the credential headers.

### How it works
1. Your backend calls [`POST /auth/tokens/user`](#tag/Access-Tokens/paths/~1auth~1tokens~1user/post) or [`POST /auth/tokens/platform`](#tag/Access-Tokens/paths/~1auth~1tokens~1platform/post) with the credential headers.
2. Connect Trade returns the `access_token` and its `expires_at` time.
3. Your backend passes the `access_token` to the browser.
4. The browser sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` instead of the credential headers, or uses the token to authenticate to the [Streaming Broker API](#tag/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication-with-an-access-token).
5. Before the token expires, the browser asks your backend for a new one.

### Token lifecycle
- **Platform access tokens** are valid for 1 hour. **User access tokens** are valid for 15 minutes.
- There are no refresh tokens. Request a new token with your credential headers before the current one expires.
- You can hold several active tokens at once. Creating a token doesn't invalidate earlier ones.
- Tokens can only be created with credential headers, not with another token.
- Deleting a user invalidates that user's tokens immediately.
- Rotating a secret stops new tokens being created with the old secret. Tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

tags.name: Streaming Broker API
tags.description:
Connect Trade provides a WebSocket streaming API for receiving order, position and balance updates.

WebSocket API is available at `wss://stream.connecttrade.com` and requires JSON encoded messages.

After connecting, client has to authenticate with client credentials or an access token (see [Authentication](#section/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication)). Following successful authentication, client must `subscribe` to topics of interest and `subscribe_user` for each platform user whose updates the session should receive. Updates for a user are delivered only while at least one session is subscribed to that user. A session authenticated with a user access token is subscribed to its user automatically.

Client implementation needs to incorporate re-connection logic for re-establishing subscriptions in the event of a disconnection.

There is a sample python implementation (`sample_stream_api_client`) available using asyncio.

## Session workflow

1. Connect to `wss://stream.connecttrade.com`
2. Send an `authenticate` message. Connection will be terminated if client is not authenticated within 30 seconds from establishing connection.
3. Send a `subscribe` message for subscribing to topics of interest.
4. Send a `subscribe_user` message for each platform user whose updates the session should receive. Updates for a user are delivered only while at least one session is subscribed to that user. Skip this step when authenticated with a user access token.
5. Receive unsolicited updates for the topics subscribed.

## Welcome message

Upon establishing a WebSocket connection, server will emit a `welcome` message. This message, **with one striking exception**, is intended to be read by humans. Its schema is subject to change and you shouldn't be expected to use it, parse it or respond to it.

The only property out of the `welcome` message that is of interest is `session_id`. Session ID can be useful for uniquely identifying a session when contacting Connect Trade support and is otherwise not used anywhere else.

```json
{
    "type": "welcome", 
    "session_id": "1e04d508-7795-4a5e-8693-2423e957061d", 
    "message": "Connected to Connect Trade WebSocket API. Please authenticate within 30 seconds or connection will be closed. If you encounter an issue during this session make sure you include value of session_id property when contacting support.", 
    "timeout_seconds": 30, 
    "required_steps": 
    [
        "1. Send authentication message with your client credentials or an access token", 
        "2. Once authenticated, you can subscribe to data feeds at anytime"
    ]
}
```

## Authentication

An `authenticate` message is the only allowed message type for newly established connections. Any other message type will be ignored at this phase.

Authentication needs to occur within the first 30 seconds of a newly established connection. Server will terminate unauthenticated connections after this period.

There are two ways to authenticate. Use one of them per connection:

| Method | What the session receives | After authenticating |
|---|---|---|
| [Client credentials](#section/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication-with-client-credentials) | Updates for any user of your platform | `subscribe` to topics, then `subscribe_user` for each user |
| [Access token](#section/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication-with-an-access-token) – platform access token | Updates for any user of your platform | `subscribe` to topics, then `subscribe_user` for each user |
| [Access token](#section/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication-with-an-access-token) – user access token | Updates for **one** user only | `subscribe` to topics. The user is subscribed automatically |

Trying to authenticate a second time, after session has already been authenticated successfully will result in a non-fatal error:
```json
{
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "Session is already authenticated"
}
```

## Authentication with client credentials

Authenticate with your platform's `client_id` and `client_secret`.

Authenticate message

```json
{
    "action": "authenticate", 
    "client_id": "your-client-id", 
    "client_secret": "your-client-secret"
}
```
- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"authenticate"`.
- `client_id` - (Required) - Your client ID.
- `client_secret` - (Required) - Your client secret.

Successful authentication

```json
{
    "type": "auth_success", 
    "message": "Authentication successful"
}
```

Unsuccessful authentication

```json
{
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "<Failure reason>"
}
```

After authenticating, send a `subscribe` message for the topics you want, and a `subscribe_user` message for each user whose updates the session should receive.

**Session limit.** The same `client_id`/`client_secret` pair may be used by more than one session at a time, up to a per-`client_id` concurrent-session cap (currently **10**). Sessions authenticated with platform access tokens for the same `client_id` count towards the same cap. Each WebSocket connection has its own per-session user-subscription limit (see [User-subscription limit](#section/Streaming-Broker-API/User-subscription-limit)), so opening additional sessions is the supported way to scale beyond it.

Authentication attempts beyond the concurrent-session cap are rejected with:

```json
{
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "Concurrent session limit (10) reached for this client_id"
}
```

## Authentication with an access token

Use this when a browser or another front end opens the WebSocket connection, so it never needs your client secret. If the connection is opened from your server, use [client credentials](#tag/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication-with-client-credentials) instead. See [Access Tokens](#tag/Access-Tokens) for when to use them and how to create them.

These tokens are not the same as the Streaming Market Data API token from `GET /connections/{connection_id}/token`. Each token works only with its own API.

Authenticate with an access token created through the REST API, instead of sending your client secret. There are two kinds of access token:
- **Platform access token**, created with [`POST /auth/tokens/platform`](#tag/Access-Tokens/paths/~1auth~1tokens~1platform/post). The session works exactly like a session authenticated with client credentials.
- **User access token**, created with [`POST /auth/tokens/user`](#tag/Access-Tokens/paths/~1auth~1tokens~1user/post). The session only receives updates for that one user. Use it when a client application connects on behalf of a single user, so the application never needs your client secret.

Send only the `access_token`. Don't send `client_id` / `client_secret` in the same message.

The token is only checked when the session authenticates. The session stays open after the token expires. You don't need to re-authenticate. Use a valid token when you open a new connection.

A token that is expired is rejected with:

```json
{
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "Access token has expired"
}
```

Any other invalid token is rejected with:

```json
{
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "Invalid access token"
}
```

### Platform access token

1. Create a token with [`POST /auth/tokens/platform`](#tag/Access-Tokens/paths/~1auth~1tokens~1platform/post).
2. Connect and send the authenticate message:

    ```json
    {
        "action": "authenticate", 
        "access_token": "your-platform-access-token"
    }
    ```
    - `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"authenticate"`.
    - `access_token` - (Required) - Your platform access token.

3. On success the server replies:

    ```json
    {
        "type": "auth_success", 
        "message": "Authentication successful"
    }
    ```

4. Send a `subscribe` message for the topics you want, and a `subscribe_user` message for each user whose updates the session should receive.

**Session limit.** Platform access token sessions count towards the same per-`client_id` cap (currently **10**) as client credential sessions.

### User access token

1. Create a token for the user with [`POST /auth/tokens/user`](#tag/Access-Tokens/paths/~1auth~1tokens~1user/post).
2. Connect and send the authenticate message:

    ```json
    {
        "action": "authenticate", 
        "access_token": "your-user-access-token"
    }
    ```
    - `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"authenticate"`.
    - `access_token` - (Required) - The user access token.

3. On success the server replies with the `user_id` the session is locked to:

    ```json
    {
        "type": "auth_success", 
        "message": "Authentication successful", 
        "user_id": "76873239-50c7-4b1c-bb1f-7dc2c9a3af36"
    }
    ```

4. Send a `subscribe` message for the topics you want. The session is already subscribed to its user, so there is no need to send `subscribe_user`.

The session is locked to that user:
- It only ever receives that user's updates.
- `subscribe_user` for any other user fails with:

    ```json
    {
        "type": "subscription_failed",
        "message": "A session authenticated with a user access token can only subscribe to its own user"
    }
    ```

- If the user is deleted, the server sends an `error` message and closes the connection with code `1008` and reason `User deleted`.

**Session limit.** Each user can have up to **5** concurrent sessions. User sessions don't count towards the per-`client_id` cap. Authentication attempts beyond the limit are rejected with:

```json
{
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "Concurrent session limit (5) reached for this user"
}
```

## Subscribing

Subscribing to topics is possible only after successfully authenticating. Available topics are:
- `orders`
- `positions`
- `balances`

Depending on your account, or your platform, or other reasons, not all topics might be available for you, or not all topics might emit updates.

Your client implementation can (and should) subscribe to more than one topic at the same time.

Subscribe message

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe", 
    "topics": ["orders", "positions", "balances"]
}
```

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"subscribe"`.
- `topics` - (Required) - A list of topics of interest. Each topic can only be referenced once (no multiple copies allowed). Topic names are case-sensitive and need to match the available topic names listed above.

You can alternatively set `topics` equal to `[ "all" ]`. This will get your session subscribed to all available topics. You need to be careful when using `[ "all" ]` as it might result in unexpected behaviour from your client if/when new topics are introduced.

Successful subscription

```json
{
    "type": "subscribed", 
    "subscription_id": "518f11fa-1b8e-485f-a7a4-c485437149e8", 
    "topics": ["orders", "positions", "balances"]
}
```

Unsuccessful subscription

```json
{
    "type": "subscription_failed",
    "message": "Error message"
}
```

## Per-user subscriptions

A per-user subscription enables update delivery for a specific platform user. Updates for a user are delivered only while at least one session is subscribed to that user. Delivery stops when the last subscribing session unsubscribes or disconnects.

Per-user subscriptions are required to receive update messages. The two steps work together:
- `subscribe` (topics) selects which message types this session is interested in.
- `subscribe_user` selects which platform users this session receives updates for.

A session may subscribe to multiple users.

A session authenticated with a [user access token](#section/Streaming-Broker-API/Authentication-with-an-access-token) is subscribed to its own user automatically and can't subscribe to other users.

### Subscribing a user

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe_user",
    "user_id": "76873239-50c7-4b1c-bb1f-7dc2c9a3af36"
}
```

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"subscribe_user"`.
- `user_id` - (Required) - The user ID to subscribe.

Successful response

```json
{
    "type": "user_subscribed",
    "user_id": "76873239-50c7-4b1c-bb1f-7dc2c9a3af36"
}
```

Subscribing the same `(session, user_id)` pair more than once is a no-op and is not counted twice against the user-subscription limit.

### Unsubscribing a user

```json
{
    "action": "unsubscribe_user",
    "user_id": "76873239-50c7-4b1c-bb1f-7dc2c9a3af36"
}
```

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"unsubscribe_user"`.
- `user_id` - (Required) - The user ID to unsubscribe.

Successful response

```json
{
    "type": "user_unsubscribed",
    "user_id": "76873239-50c7-4b1c-bb1f-7dc2c9a3af36"
}
```

Unsubscribing a `(session, user_id)` pair that is not currently subscribed is a no-op.

### Automatic cleanup on disconnect

When a session disconnects, all of its per-user subscriptions are released as if `unsubscribe_user` had been called for each one. If a user has been subscribed by multiple sessions, update delivery for that user continues until the last subscribing session releases it.

### User-subscription limit

Each WebSocket session can subscribe to up to **500** distinct platform users via `subscribe_user`. Attempting to subscribe a user beyond this limit fails with a `subscription_failed` response.

If you need to receive updates for more than 500 users concurrently, open additional WebSocket connections (the same `client_id`/`client_secret` pair may be used by multiple sessions) and split your `subscribe_user` calls across them. Each session has its own independent limit.

### Failures

Failed requests (e.g., missing `user_id`, unknown `user_id` on this platform, unauthenticated session, or user-subscription limit reached) are reported with:

```json
{
    "type": "subscription_failed",
    "message": "Error message"
}
```

## Testing connection state

The API allows probing the state of a connection using `ping` messages. Server will respond to `ping` messages with `pong` messages. Server will not emit `ping` messages itself.

Sample client implementation (ab)uses `ping` messages for measuring round-trip latency (RRT) with the server.

Ping message (client request)

```json
{
    "action": "ping", 
    "seq": 1
}
```
- `action` - (Required) - Always `"ping"`.
- `seq` - (Optional) - An integer. Server will copy value of `seq` on respective `pong` message. This allows client implementations to identify the original `ping` message the server-side emitted `pong` is a response for.

Pong message (server response)

```json
{
    "type": "pong", 
    "seq": 1
}
```

## Update examples

tags.name: Streaming Market Data API
tags.description:
Connect Trade provides a WebSocket Market Data API for retrieving real-time and historical market data.

The Market Data API is available at `wss://mdstream.connecttrade.com` and uses JSON-encoded messages for communication.

**Important**: Authentication for the Market Data API is per user and per user connection. Each connection represents a 
user's authenticated link to a specific broker that provides market data to the user. The `connection_id` specifies which
broker the market data will be retrieved from. The platform requests market data on behalf of the user by first obtaining 
an access token for a specific connection, then uses that token to authenticate the WebSocket connection for retrieving
market data.

After opening the websocket connection, the client must authenticate using the previously acquired access token. Following 
successful authentication, the client can then `subscribe` to market data feeds for receiving real-time market data updates, 
or send `snapshot` messages for retrieving historical market data.


## Session workflow

1. Obtain an access token for the user connection by calling `GET https://api.connecttrade.com/connections/{connection_id}/token`
2. Connect to `wss://mdstream.connecttrade.com`
3. Send an `authenticate` message using the access token. The connection will be terminated if the client is not authenticated within 30 seconds of establishing the connection.
4. Send a `subscribe` message to subscribe to market data streams, or a `snapshot` message to retrieve historical market data.
5. Receive updates for the subscribed symbols or responses to historical market data requests.

## Authentication

An `authenticate` message is the only allowed message type for newly established connections. Any other message type will be rejected during this phase.

Authentication must occur within the first 30 seconds of establishing a connection. The server will terminate unauthenticated connections after this period.

To authenticate, you need to provide an `access_token` obtained from the connections token endpoint.

## Obtaining an access token

Before connecting to the Market Data API WebSocket, obtain an access token for the specific user and connection by calling the following REST endpoint:

```
GET https://api.connecttrade.com/connections/{connection_id}/token
```

The following headers must be provided:
- `client-id`
- `client-secret`
- `user-id`
- `user-secret`

This endpoint returns an access token that can be used to authenticate WebSocket connections on behalf of the user for retrieving market data from the 
broker associated with the specified connection. Generated access token is valid for 24 hours and a new one must be obtained after (or before) it expires. 
Generating a new token invalidates all previously generated tokens.

While generating a new token invalidates any previously generated tokens (they cannot any more be used for authenticating further websocket connections), it 
does not invalidate (force disconnection of) currently established websocket connections/subscriptions that authenticated using a previously generated access 
token.

Instead, any currently authenticated (and still running) websocket connections, which authenticated using a now outdated access token, will be forcefully 
disconnected by the server upon the first use of the newly generated access token. This behaviour enables the platform to obtain and distribute the new 
access token, without disrupting existing websocket connections in the process. Previously established websocket connections will be forcefully terminated 
only after the new access token is used for the first time, allowing for a smoother end-user experience.

**Important**: A platform user with more than one broker connections can have as many valid and non-expired access tokens as the broker connections available. 
However, only one of his access tokens can be in use at any one time. Each user, regardless of the count of available broker connections, can only be 
actively consuming market data originating from a single source/broker. Every time a user authenticates using an access token, the server forcefully disconnects
any websocket connections that use a different access token, even if that other access token is still valid, non-expired and still usable.


## Authenticate message

Once you have acquired an access token, use it to authenticate the WebSocket connection:

```json
{
    "action": "authenticate", 
    "access_token": "user-access-token", 
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```
- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"authenticate"`.
- `access_token` - (Required) - The access token obtained from the connections token endpoint.
- `request_id` - (Required) - A unique identifier for this request, useful for tracking and debugging.

**Important**: A platform user can have multiple websocket connections established, using the same access token. However, all connections must 
originate from the same IP address. Every time a user authenticates from an IP address, the server forcefully disconnects any other websocket 
connections of the user that originate from a different IP address.


Successful authentication

```json
{
    "type": "auth_success", 
    "message": "Authentication successful", 
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "session_id": "1e04d508-7795-4a5e-8693-2423e957061d"
}
```

Unsuccessful authentication

```json
{
    "type": "error",
    "error_code": "auth_error",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "message": "<Failure reason>"
}
```

## Subscribing

Subscribing to market data channels is possible only after successful authentication.

Bars subscription message

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe", 
    "channel": "bars",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "interval": "1m",
    "session": "USEqCore",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "backfill_nbars": 60
}
```

Trades subscription message

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe", 
    "channel": "trades",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "session": "USEqCore",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```      

Quotes subscription message

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe", 
    "channel": "quotes",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```   

Depth (Level 2) subscription message

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe", 
    "channel": "depth",
    "symbol": "MSFT",
    "n_levels": 2,
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```   

Options Chain subscription message

```json
{
    "action": "subscribe", 
    "channel": "options_chain",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "greeks": true,
    "expiration": "2026-01-30",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```   

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"subscribe"`.
- `channel` - (Required) - The market data channel to subscribe to. Available values are `"bars"`, `"trades"`, `"quotes"`, `"depth"` and `"options_chain"`.
- `symbol` - (Required) - The market symbol to receive data for.
  - Crypto symbols must use BASE/QUOTE format (e.g. BTC/USD, ETH/USDT).
  - Futures symbols use [ROOT][M][YY] symbology with a 2-digit year (e.g. ESU26, ZNH27, MESZ26). 
- `interval` - (Optional) - Required when `channel` is `"bars"`. The time interval for the data. Format is a number followed by a case-sensitive unit: `m` for minute, `h` for hour, `d` for day, `w` for week, `M` for month, `y` for year. Examples: `"1m"`, `"5m"`, `"4h"`, `"1d"`, `"1w"`, `"1M"`, `"1y"`. `"4h"` and `"240m"` are the same subscription.
- `session` - (Optional) - Available only for `"bars"` and `"trades"`. Market data session to subscribe to. Defaults to `"BrokerDefault"` if not provided. Ignored for non-equity symbols. 
  Available values are:
  - `"BrokerDefault"`: Whatever session is the default for this broker.
  - `"USEqCore"`: Core/cash session data only.
  - `"USEqPreMkt"`: Pre-market and core/cash session data.
  - `"USEqPostMkt"`: Core/cash and post-market session data.
  - `"USEqPreAndPostMkt"`: Pre-market, core/cash and post-market session data.
  - `"USEq24Hour"`: 24 hours data.
- `request_id` - (Required) - A unique identifier for this request, useful for tracking and debugging.
- `backfill_nbars` - (Optional) - Only available for `"bars"`. Number of past bars to return. Each broker has different limits on how many bars can be requested for the specified `interval` value.
  Defaults to `0` if not specified.
- `n_levels` - (Optional) - Only available for `"depth"`. Number of price levels to receive for both bid and ask sides. Must be between 1 and 10.
  Defaults to `5` if not specified.
- `greeks` - (Optional) - Only available for `"options_chain"`. When set to `true`, the response will include Greek values (delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho) for each option in the chain.
  Defaults to `false` if not specified.
- `expiration` - (Required) - Only available for `"options_chain"`. The expiration date of the options to include in the chain, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

**Notes**:
1. Not all brokers offer all possible `interval` combinations.
2. Not all brokers offer all possible `session` values.

Successful subscription response

```json
{
    "type": "subscription_success",
    "message": "Subscription successful",
    "broker": "alpaca",
    "channel": "bars",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "interval": "1m",
    "session": "USEqCore",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "sub_id": "1"
}
```

- `type` - Response type: `"subscription_success"`.
- `message` - Confirmation text message.
- `broker` - The broker for the subscription.
- `channel` - The market data channel subscribed to.
- `symbol` - The symbol subscribed to.
- `interval` - The time interval for the subscription. Only populated when `channel` is `"bars"`.
- `session` - The trading session this subscription will be providing data from. Only populated when `channel` is `"bars"` or `"trades"`.
- `request_id` - The request ID from the original subscription request.
- `sub_id` - Unique subscription identifier assigned by the server (auto-incremented integer).

**Note**: `backfill_nbars` is not considered part of the subscription. It is not returned as part of the `subscription_success` message, nor is listed within `subscriptions_list` messages.

After subscribing, you will start receiving real-time updates for the specified channel, symbol and interval (where applicable).

Bar update example
```json
{
  "o": "200.00",
  "h": "201.00",
  "l": "199.50",
  "c": "200.37",
  "v": "1500",
  "ts": "1767991120000000000",
  "st": "c",
  "sub_id": "1"
}
```

- `o` - Open price.
- `h` - High price.
- `l` - Low price.
- `c` - Close price.
- `v` - Volume.
- `ts` - Timestamp of the bar, in nanoseconds since Unix epoch.
- `st` - Status of the bar: `"c"` for closed, `"o"` for open.
- `sub_id` - The subscription identifier this update belongs to.

Trade update example
```json
{
  "p":"221.12",
  "s":"100",
  "ts":"1767992118000000000",
  "sub_id":"7",
  "n":""
}
```

- `p` - Trade price.
- `s` - Trade size.
- `n` - Venue of the trade. Not all brokers provide this information.
- `ts` - Timestamp of the trade in the resolution provided by the broker, expressed as nanoseconds since Unix epoch.
- `sub_id` - The subscription identifier this update belongs to.

Quote update example
```json
{
  "bp": "213.05",
  "bs": "100",
  "ap": "213.38",
  "as": "300",
  "ts": "1767992399000000000",
  "sub_id": "1"
}
```

- `bp` - Bid price.
- `bs` - Bid size.
- `ap` - Ask price.
- `as` - Ask size.
- `ts` - Timestamp of the trade in the resolution provided by the broker, expressed as nanoseconds since Unix epoch.
- `sub_id` - The subscription identifier this update belongs to.

Depth (Level 2) update example

```json
{
  "b": [
    ["461.33", "40", "1", "ARCX", "1768478492000000000"],
    ["461.25", "40", "1", "EDGX", "1768478454000000000"],
    ["461.25", "3", "1", "NSDQ", "1768478414000000000"]
  ],
  "a": [
    ["461.5", "40", "1", "ARCX", "1768478444000000000"],
    ["461.5", "497", "1", "NSDQ", "1768478291000000000"],
    ["461.62", "50", "1", "NSDQ", "1768478491000000000"]
  ],
  "sub_id": "1"
}
```

- `type` - Update type: `"depth_update"`.
- `b` - Array of bid levels. Each level is an array containing:
  - `[0]` - Price.
  - `[1]` - Size (number of shares).
  - `[2]` - Number of orders.
  - `[3]` - Exchange code.
  - `[4]` - Timestamp in nanoseconds since Unix epoch.
- `a` - Array of ask levels. Same structure as bid levels.
- `sub_id` - The subscription identifier this update belongs to.

Options Chain update example

```json
{
  "delta": "-0.2115",
  "gamma": "0.0171",
  "theta": "-0.1537",
  "rho": "-0.0241",
  "vega": "0.1545",
  "iv": "0.3176",
  "ask": "2.1",
  "bid": "1.98",
  "mid": "2.04",
  "ask_size": "20",
  "bid_size": "11",
  "close": "2.23",
  "high": "2.91",
  "last": "2.23",
  "low": "1.97",
  "net_change": "0.12",
  "net_change_pct": "0.0569",
  "open": "2.33",
  "previous_close": "2.11",
  "volume": "121",
  "side": "Put",
  "legs": [
    {
      "sym": "AAPL 260130P247.5",
      "strike_price": "247.5",
      "expiration": "2026-01-30T00:00:00Z",
      "option_type": "Put",
      "asset_type": "StockOption"
    }
  ],
  "sub_id": "1"
}
```

- `delta` - The rate of change of the option value with respect to changes in the underlying asset's price.
- `gamma` - The rate of change in delta over time.
- `theta` - The measure of time decay of the option.
- `rho` - The rate of change of the option value with respect to interest rates.
- `vega` - The measure of an option's sensitivity to volatility.
- `iv` - Implied volatility.
- `ask` - Ask price.
- `bid` - Bid price.
- `mid` - Mid price between bid and ask.
- `ask_size` - Ask size.
- `bid_size` - Bid size.
- `close` - Closing price.
- `high` - High price of the session.
- `last` - Last traded price.
- `low` - Low price of the session.
- `net_change` - Net change from previous close.
- `net_change_pct` - Net change percentage from previous close.
- `open` - Opening price.
- `previous_close` - Previous session's closing price.
- `volume` - Trading volume.
- `side` - Option side (`"Put"`, `"Call"` or `"Both"`).
- `legs` - Array of option leg details.
  - `sym` - Option symbol.
  - `strike_price` - Strike price of the option.
  - `expiration` - Expiration date and time in ISO 8601 format.
  - `option_type` - Type of option (`"Put"` or `"Call"`).
  - `asset_type` - Asset type.
- `sub_id` - The subscription identifier this update belongs to.


## List active subscriptions

To list your active subscriptions, send the following message:

```json
{
    "action": "list_subscriptions", 
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"list_subscriptions"`.
- `request_id` - (Required) - A unique identifier for this request.

Successful response

```json
{
    "type": "subscriptions_list", 
    "subscriptions": [
        {
            "broker": "TRADESTATION",
            "channel": "bars",
            "symbol": "AAPL",
            "interval": "1m",
            "session": "USEqCore",
            "sub_id": "1"
        },
        {
            "broker": "TRADESTATION",
            "channel": "bars",
            "symbol": "TSLA",
            "interval": "5m",
            "session": "USEqCore",
            "sub_id": "2"
        },
        {
            "broker": "TRADESTATION",
            "channel": "trades",
            "symbol": "AMD",
            "interval": "",
            "session": "USEq24Hour",
            "sub_id":"3"
        },
        {
            "broker": "TRADESTATION",
            "channel": "quotes",
            "symbol": "MSFT",
            "interval": "",
            "session": "",
            "sub_id":"4"
        }              
    ],
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```

- `type` - Response type: `"subscriptions_list"`.
- `subscriptions` - Array of active subscriptions.
  - `broker` - The broker for the subscription.
  - `channel` - The market data channel (e.g., `"bars"`).
  - `symbol` - The symbol being subscribed to.
  - `interval` - The time interval for the subscription. Always empty for trade and quote subscriptions.
  - `session` - The trading session this subscription provides data from. Always empty for quote subscriptions.
  - `sub_id` - Unique subscription identifier (auto-incremented by server).
- `request_id` - The request ID from the original request.

## Unsubscribing

To unsubscribe from a market data feed, send the following message:

```json
{
    "action": "unsubscribe", 
    "sub_id": "1",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id"
}
```

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"unsubscribe"`.
- `sub_id` - (Required) - The subscription identifier assigned by the server to the subscription.
- `request_id` - (Required) - A unique identifier for this request.

Successful unsubscription

```json
{
    "type": "unsubscription_success", 
    "message": "Unsubscription successful",
    "broker": "TRADESTATION",
    "channel": "bars",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "interval": "1m",
    "session": "USEqCore",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "sub_id": "1"
}
```

- `type` - Response type: `"unsubscription_success"`.
- `message` - Confirmation message.
- `broker` - The broker for the unsubscribed feed.
- `channel` - The market data channel that was unsubscribed from.
- `symbol` - The symbol that was unsubscribed from.
- `interval` - The time interval that was unsubscribed from. Always empty for trade, quote and options_chain subscriptions.
- `session` - The trading session the subscription provided data from. Always empty for quote and options_chain subscriptions.
- `request_id` - The request ID from the original request.
- `sub_id` - The subscription identifier that was removed (originally assigned by the server).

## Requesting historical market data

Bars snapshot request

To retrieve historical bar data for a specific time range, send the following message:

```json
{
    "action": "snapshot",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "start_time": "2025-06-30T09:30:00Z",
    "end_time": "2025-06-30T16:00:00Z",
    "data_type": "bars",
    "interval": "1m"
}
```

- `action` - (Required) - Needs to be `"snapshot"`.
- `request_id` - (Required) - A unique identifier for this request.
- `symbol` - (Required) - The market symbol to retrieve data for.
- `start_time` - (Required) - The start time for the historical data range in ISO 8601 format (UTC).
- `end_time` - (Required) - The end time for the historical data range in ISO 8601 format (UTC).
- `data_type` - (Required) - The type of data to retrieve. Currently supported value is `"bars"`.
- `interval` - (Required) - The time interval for the bars. Format is a number followed by a case-sensitive unit: `m` for minute, `h` for hour, `d` for day, `w` for week, `M` for month, `y` for year. Examples: `"5m"`, `"4h"`, `"1d"`.

Bars snapshot response

```json
{
    "type": "snapshot_response",
    "request_id": "unique-request-id",
    "symbol": "AAPL",
    "data_type": "bars",
    "interval": "1m",
    "start_time": "2025-06-30T09:30:00Z",
    "end_time": "2025-06-30T16:00:00Z",
    "data": [
        {
            "o": "200",
            "h": "201",
            "l": "199.5",
            "c": "200.37",
            "v": "1500",
            "ts": "1751275800000000000",
            "st": "c",
            "ev": "b",
            "sym": "AAPL"
        },
        {
            "o": "200.37",
            "h": "201.5",
            "l": "200",
            "c": "201.25",
            "v": "2100",
            "ts": "1751275860000000000",
            "st": "c",
            "ev": "b",
            "sym": "AAPL"
        }
    ]
}
```

- `type` - Response type: `"snapshot_response"`.
- `request_id` - The request ID from the original request.
- `symbol` - The symbol for the returned data.
- `data_type` - The type of data returned: `"bars"`.
- `interval` - The time interval for the bars.
- `start_time` - The start time of the requested range.
- `end_time` - The end time of the requested range.
- `data` - Array of historical bar data. Each bar contains:
  - `o` - Open price.
  - `h` - High price.
  - `l` - Low price.
  - `c` - Close price.
  - `v` - Volume.
  - `ts` - Start time of the bar, in Unix nanoseconds.
  - `st` - Status of the bar: `"c"` for closed, `"o"` for open.
  - `ev` - Event type: `"b"` for bar.
  - `sym` - The symbol.

post.description:
Creates a connection URL that re-authenticates an existing connection with its broker. Use it to recover a connection with status BROKEN.

The user must log in to the same broker and environment and select the same accounts. The connection keeps its connection_id and accounts, and its status becomes ACTIVE.

After a successful repair, the system redirects to the redirect_url and includes the connection_id as a URL parameter.

Example (success):
https://example.com/callbacks/success?connection_id=7fe430be-4b21-4e34-b335-3480017a7165

If redirect_url is not provided, the user will remain on the Connect Trade platform.

If the repair fails, the connection is left unchanged and the system redirects to redirect_on_error_url (or to redirect_url if redirect_on_error_url is not provided) and includes error details as URL parameters. To change the connected accounts, delete the connection and create a new one.

Example (error):
https://example.com/callbacks/error?error=connection_repair_failed&error_details=The+selected+accounts+do+not+match+the+connection+being+repaired.

Filter by transaction types (comma-separated list).

Available transaction types: ACAT, ACCOUNT_TRANSFER, DEPOSIT, DIVIDEND, FEE, FILL, INTEREST, JOURNAL_ENTRY, MISC, OPTION_EXPIRATION, OPTION_ASSIGNMENT, OPTION_EXERCISE, REI, TAX, WITHDRAWAL

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Filter transactions from this timestamp (ISO 8601 format).

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Filter transactions up to this timestamp (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of transactions to return

parameters.name: next_cursor
parameters.description: Cursor for forward pagination. Pass the next_cursor value from the previous response to retrieve the next set of results. Mutually exclusive with prev_cursor—only one cursor parameter may be supplied per request.

parameters.name: prev_cursor
parameters.description: Cursor for backward pagination. Pass the prev_cursor value from the current response to retrieve the previous set of results. Mutually exclusive with next_cursor—only one cursor parameter may be supplied per request.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort parameter (field:direction). Only a single sort field is allowed at a time.

Supported sort fields:
  - transaction_time
  - trade_date

ConnectionStatus.description:
The health status of the connection.

- `ACTIVE` - The connection is usable.
- `BROKEN` - The broker has definitively rejected the connection's credentials (e.g. they were revoked or expired). Requests that need to reach the broker through this connection (creating, replacing or cancelling orders) are rejected with `409 Conflict`. To recover, repair the connection with `POST /connections/{connection_id}/repair`.

redirect_url.description:
The URL to redirect the user after successful authentication. This field is optional.
If provided, the system will redirect to this URL with the newly created connection_id as a URL parameter.
If provided, a valid URL is required. Empty strings are not allowed.
`https://` is required for non-localhost hosts. `http://` is allowed only for `localhost` during development.
If not provided, the user will remain on the Connect Trade platform.

The URL to redirect the user when an error occurs during the connection process. This field is optional.
If provided, the same validation rules apply as `redirect_url`.
If not provided and `redirect_url` is provided, the system will redirect to `redirect_url`. Otherwise, the user will remain on the Connect Trade platform.

If provided, the system will redirect to this URL with the repaired connection_id as a URL parameter.
The same validation rules apply as `redirect_url` in connection creation.
If not provided, the user will remain on the Connect Trade platform.

account_id.description: Account ID. The unique identifier for the account associated with the order.

side.description:
Order side.

**Equities, futures and crypto**: Send `BUY`, `SELL`, or `SELL_SHORT`. Connect Trade marks the side correctly for whichever broker you're routing to, using your current position to determine open/close intent when needed.

Explicit variants (`BUY_TO_OPEN`, `BUY_TO_CLOSE`, `BUY_TO_COVER`, `SELL_TO_OPEN`, `SELL_TO_CLOSE`) are also accepted and passed through as-is.

**Options**: `BUY_TO_OPEN`, `BUY_TO_CLOSE`, `SELL_TO_OPEN`, `SELL_TO_CLOSE`

**Multileg**: This field is ignored.

*Note:* `side` *is not modified on notional orders, or on the equity/crypto leg of an order while a notional order is still open.*

order_qty.description: Order quantity. The number of shares, contracts, or units to buy or sell.

order_notional.description: Order notional. The total notional value of the order.

order_type.description: Order type. Specifies the type of order execution. Must be omitted when `complex_order_parameters.order_class` is `OCO`.

order_tif.description: Order time in force (TIF). Indicates how long the order remains active.

order_limit_price.description: Order price. The price at which to execute the order. Must be omitted when `complex_order_parameters.order_class` is `OCO`.

price_effect.description:
Indicates the direction money will flow in relation to the account as a result of this order. 
Required by some brokers for some order types and/or instruments. 
Any value will be ignored if not required by the specific broker/order type/instrument combination.

symbol.description:
Order symbol. The ticker or identifier of the security to trade.

- Options symbols must use OCC symbology (e.g. MSFT251024C00290000).
- Crypto symbols must use BASE/QUOTE format (e.g. BTC/USD, ETH/USDT).
- Futures symbols use [ROOT][M][YY] symbology with a 2-digit year (e.g. ESU26, ZNH27, MESZ26). 
  - Continuous contracts and spread symbols are not accepted. 
  - Connect Trade root symbols are [listed here](https://connecttrade.com/docs#symbology). 
  - Connect Trade does not validate expirations or per-product broker availability. The broker is the authority for whether a given contract is tradable. Clients should expect a broker-sourced rejection rather than a Connect Trade validation error for an unavailable contract.

Multileg: This field does not apply to multileg orders and will be ignored if included.

instrument.description: Order instrument. Specifies the type of instrument. Use `MLEG_OPT` for a multileg order and populate the `legs` array.

exec_dest.description: Execution destination. Optionally specifies the venue or exchange.

stop_price.description: Stop price. Required for stop and stop-limit orders. Must be omitted when `complex_order_parameters.order_class` is `OCO`.

legs.description: Array of legs for a multileg order. Required for multileg orders. Multileg orders can have a minimum of 2 legs and a maximum of 4 legs.

symbol.description: Leg symbol. The ticker or identifier of the option security for this leg using OCC symbology.

action.description: Conveys the intent of the leg trade.

ratio.description: Ratio of this leg in relation to the `order_qty`.

complex_order_parameters.description:
Complex order parameters. Omit for a simple order. How the top-level fields are read depends on `order_class`:

- `BRACKET`: the top-level fields describe the entry order. Both `take_profit` and `stop_loss` are required. The exit orders are placed on the reverse side of the entry when it fills. When one exit fills, the other is cancelled.
- `OTO`: the top-level fields describe the entry order. Exactly one of `take_profit` or `stop_loss` is required. The exit order is placed on the reverse side of the entry when it fills.
- `OCO`: no entry order. `side` is the side both orders execute on (`SELL` protects a long position, `BUY` a short position). Both `take_profit` and `stop_loss` are required. `order_type`, `order_limit_price` and `stop_price` must not be sent at the top level. When one order fills, the other is cancelled.
